issues.t: Front air springs leak and the car sags
issues.sym: After sitting overnight the front end (or one corner) is noticeably lower, the car may scrape on driveways, and the ride feels harsh or bouncy until the system pumps back up.
issues.why: The Mark VIII rides on rubber air bags built into each strut. With age the rubber dries out and cracks, so the springs slowly lose air.
issues.next: Check whether one corner sits low after parking. A badly sagging car can rub its tires and handle poorly, so have the air struts tested and replace leaking ones, ideally in pairs. Many owners switch to a coil-spring conversion kit.

issues.t: Air suspension compressor wears out
issues.sym: The suspension warning lamp comes on, you hear the compressor running often or for a long time, or the car never reaches normal ride height.
issues.why: Leaking air springs make the compressor run far more than it was designed to, which wears it out. A clogged or failed drier can add to the problem.
issues.next: Find and fix the leak first; a new compressor on a leaking system will fail again. Turn off the air suspension switch in the trunk before jacking the car up.

issues.t: Front height sensor link breaks
issues.sym: The car sits too high or too low at the front, or the suspension warning lamp comes on.
issues.why: The small ball stud on the front ride-height sensor link can snap, so the air suspension computer no longer knows how high the car is sitting.
issues.next: Have the height sensors and their links inspected before replacing the air springs. Ford issued service bulletins on this part.

issues.t: Shudder at highway speed from torque converter
issues.sym: A brief shake or rumble, like driving over rumble strips, during light throttle at roughly 40 to 60 mph.
issues.why: The torque converter clutch in the 4R70W automatic engages and slips. Fluid that has broken down from heat makes it worse, and a worn converter is the worst case.
issues.next: Ford's fix was a complete fluid drain including the converter and a refill with Mercon V. If the shudder returns, have the converter checked. An added transmission cooler helps in hot climates.

issues.t: Harsh or banging 1-2 shift
issues.sym: The shift from first to second gear feels like a hard thump or bang, especially when accelerating gently.
issues.why: The 1-2 accumulator piston in the 4R70W is a known weak point. When it wears, the shift is no longer cushioned.
issues.next: Have it repaired soon. Owners report that driving on with a harsh 1-2 shift can damage the transmission.

issues.t: Late or missing 2-3 shift when cold
issues.sym: On a cold morning the car stays in second gear too long or will not shift into third, and the check engine light may come on with code P0782.
issues.why: Ford bulletins describe a 2-3 shift fault on 4R70W transmissions built in 1997 and 1998.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a shop to check the Ford service bulletins for your build date before agreeing to a rebuild.

issues.t: Clunk when shifting into reverse
issues.sym: A hard clunk or jolt when you move the shifter into reverse.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for harsh reverse engagement on certain 1998 4R70W transmissions.
issues.next: Have the fluid level checked and ask a shop about the Ford bulletin. Also check the engine and transmission mounts.

issues.t: Car slips into neutral while driving
issues.sym: On the highway the engine suddenly revs freely as if the car shifted to neutral, then may return to normal.
issues.why: A failing manual lever position sensor on the side of the transmission can wrongly tell the computer the shifter is in neutral.
issues.next: Losing drive at speed is dangerous. Pull over safely and have the sensor tested. Check it before assuming the transmission has failed.

issues.t: Vibration or drone above 60 mph
issues.sym: A vibration through the floor or a low droning noise that starts around 60 mph and grows with speed.
issues.why: These cars use a two-piece driveshaft that can be out of balance or have too much runout. The car is also very sensitive to wheel and tire balance.
issues.next: Have the tires balanced first. If that does not help, have the driveshaft checked for runout and balance. Many owners fit a one-piece balanced shaft.

issues.t: HID low beam goes dark
issues.sym: One low-beam headlight flickers, turns pink or goes out completely, making night driving hard.
issues.why: The Mark VIII uses early high-intensity discharge (HID) headlamps. The bulb or its ballast fails with age, and exact replacement bulbs became hard to find.
issues.next: Do not drive at night with a dead low beam. Have the bulb and ballast tested. Some owners use a dealer-approved conversion when original parts are not available.

issues.t: Headlight lenses cloud or collect moisture
issues.sym: The headlight lenses look hazy or yellow, or water droplets form inside, and light output drops.
issues.why: The plastic lenses oxidize with age, and some housings let condensation in.
issues.next: Have the lenses restored or the housings replaced, then have the headlight aim checked.

issues.t: Outside door handle snaps
issues.sym: The outside door handle breaks off or goes limp, and the door will not open from outside or will not latch.
issues.why: The handle is made of a weak metal and the long, heavy coupe door puts a lot of load on it.
issues.next: Get it fixed promptly. A door that cannot be opened from outside can trap a passenger in an emergency.

issues.t: Heater core leaks
issues.sym: A sweet coolant smell inside the car, a foggy film on the windshield, damp carpet on the passenger side, or coolant level dropping.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin on heater core leaks for these cars.
issues.next: Coolant vapor fogs the glass and the leak can lead to overheating, so check the coolant level and have the heater core pressure-tested.

issues.t: Cruise control switch can overheat and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. In some cases a burning smell or smoke from the engine bay, even with the car parked.
issues.why: The cruise control shut-off switch on the brake master cylinder can leak brake fluid internally, overheat and burn.
issues.next: Have a Lincoln dealer check this recall with your VIN. The fix is free and adds a fused wiring harness.

issues.t: Long crank or stall on cold starts
issues.sym: The engine cranks for a long time before starting, idles roughly when cold, or stalls soon after a cold start.
issues.why: Ford bulletins tie this to a sticking idle air control valve and engine computer calibration.
issues.next: Have the idle air control valve cleaned or replaced and ask the shop to check for updated engine computer software.

issues.t: Hard start when parked on a hill with low fuel
issues.sym: The engine cranks a long time or will not start when parked on a slope with less than a quarter tank.
issues.why: Ford bulletins describe fuel starvation at the pump when the tank is low and the car is tilted.
issues.next: Keep the tank above a quarter full. If it happens often, ask a shop about the Ford bulletin.

issues.t: Anti-theft system blocks starting
issues.sym: The engine cranks but will not start, or will not crank, and the theft light on the dash flashes.
issues.why: The passive anti-theft system cannot read the chip in the key. Damaged keys, unprogrammed copies, or a magnetic key fob on the same ring can block the signal.
issues.next: Remove other keys and fobs from the ring and try your spare key. If it still will not start, have the anti-theft codes read before replacing the starter or fuel pump.

issues.t: Rattle from cam chain tensioners at start-up
issues.sym: A clattering or rattling from the engine for a few seconds right after a morning start.
issues.why: Oil drains out of the secondary timing chain tensioners overnight, so the chains are loose until oil pressure builds.
issues.next: If the noise fades within seconds it is usually not harmful, but a rattle that lasts or gets louder should be checked, since worn chain parts can fail.

issues.t: Misfire from ignition coil boots or worn plugs
issues.sym: Rough idle, stumbling or a shake when accelerating, and a check engine light that may flash.
issues.why: The spark plugs sit deep in the heads. Worn plugs and cracked coil boots that leak spark are common by 60,000 to 70,000 miles.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.

issues.t: Check engine light from camshaft sensor wiring
issues.sym: The check engine light is on with code P0340, sometimes with hard starting.
issues.why: Ford found that the wiring at the camshaft position sensor connector can be damaged, so the computer loses the cam signal.
issues.next: Have the connector and wiring inspected before replacing the sensor itself.

issues.t: Hesitation from a dirty mass airflow sensor
issues.sym: Hesitation or stalling, rough running, poor fuel economy, or a check engine light.
issues.why: The mass airflow sensor measures incoming air; dirt or oil on the sensing element makes the readings wrong.
issues.next: Have the sensor checked. A dirty sensor can often be cleaned; a failed one is replaced as an assembly.

issues.t: Steering wheel shakes when braking
issues.sym: The steering wheel or brake pedal pulses when slowing down from highway speed.
issues.why: The heavy car is hard on its brakes, and the rotors develop uneven thickness. Ford issued bulletins on diagnosing brake vibration.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured and replaced or machined, and use quality pads. Owners note the brakes wear faster than on lighter cars.

issues.t: Front ball joint can wear and separate
issues.sym: Clunking from the front over bumps, wandering steering, or uneven tire wear. In the worst case the wheel can collapse at low speed.
issues.why: On high-mileage cars the front ball joints wear out, and owners have reported joints breaking.
issues.next: Clunks from the front end need prompt attention. Have the ball joints and control arms checked, and stop driving if the steering feels loose.

issues.t: Blower motor chirps or squeaks
issues.sym: A chirping or squeaking noise from behind the dash when the fan is on low speed.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for blower motors that squeak at low speeds.
issues.next: Not a safety issue. Have the blower motor checked and replaced if the noise bothers you.

issues.t: Musty smell from the vents
issues.sym: A musty or mildew smell when the A/C or heater first comes on.
issues.why: Moisture left on the A/C evaporator lets mold grow. Ford issued a bulletin for this.
issues.next: Replace the cabin air path filters if fitted and have an evaporator cleaning treatment done. Make sure the A/C drain is clear.

issues.t: Auto-dimming mirror turns yellow or leaks
issues.sym: The driver's outside mirror looks foggy or yellow, or a liquid stain spreads across it.
issues.why: The gel used to dim the mirror leaks out of the glass as it ages.
issues.next: A dim mirror cuts visibility, so replace the mirror glass. A plain glass insert is another option.

issues.t: Rear window seal bubbles or lifts
issues.sym: The rubber trim around the rear window bubbles or lifts, and water may get in.
issues.why: The seal is bonded to the glass and cannot be replaced on its own.
issues.next: Have it resealed with a proper adhesive before water damages the trunk or interior. Replacing the glass is a much bigger job.

issues.t: Rear sway bar cracks from inside rust
issues.sym: A clunk or rattle from the rear over bumps, or more body roll in turns.
issues.why: The rear anti-roll bar is hollow and can rust from the inside until it cracks, especially in salt states.
issues.next: Have the rear sway bar and its links inspected and replace a cracked bar.

issues.t: False door-ajar warning
issues.sym: The door-ajar message stays on even though all doors are closed, and interior lights may stay on and drain the battery.
issues.why: The switch built into the door latch sticks or wears.
issues.next: Cleaning and lubricating the latch often helps for a while. If it keeps coming back, replace the latch switch.
